Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Implement findings from your read-only audit. Opus lane is present as code, not literal 'Opus' strings; ignore provenance grep mismatch. Exclusive ownership: evals/app/judges.ts, stats.ts, arize.ts, stats.test.ts, evaluators.test.ts, and agreement.ts/reports.ts only if needed for consistent denominators. You are not alone; do not revert other edits. Do not edit run.ts, suites/*.ts, README.md (coordinator owns those). Fix (a) jevShare must not drop missing/failed items to inflate score or denominator; preserve full expected item list/errors; (b) clustered all-zero/all-one confidence intervals must use independent clusters, invariant under within-cluster duplication; (c) Arize quality metrics and local reports must share conditional quality denominator semantics: use harness execution success separately, do not invent zero on every quality metric for failed case. Arize rectangular limitations may require label-only nullable metrics with explicit status; avoid breaking actual numeric quality where all cases apply. Add focused regression tests. Existing stats/evaluator tests pass but have no negative regression cases above. Review current full code rather than assume lacking Opus. No paid APIs. Run relevant tests, report exact changed files and semantics so I can update docs. Coordinator separately fixes upload durability, malformed per-suite verdict handling, and Clairic symmetric uncertainty. Prior findings in full: upload before write loses paid outputs (run.ts525), malformed rewrite/rubric/research verdict ->zero, low-confidence agreeing Clairic kept while disagreement excluded (research.ts433), jevShare partial drops, boundary intervals use row n, Arize replaces failed rows zero but local excludes quality. Preserve separate score/coverage. No Fable.
I’ll review the current aggregation and reporting code, fix the three denominator issues within the assigned files, and add focused regression tests without calling paid APIs.

The shared code confirms all three issues. `jevShare` averages only the returned items; boundary intervals use the row count; and Arize fills failed cases with quality zeros. I’ll make incomplete Jev aggregates unscored while retaining their expected items and errors, use cluster counts at the interval boundary, and keep harness success separate from conditional quality scores.

All 42 targeted tests pass, including the new negative cases. I also fixed repeated-run averaging: failed runs no longer contribute quality values, and a failed first run no longer causes agreement reports to exclude a later successful result. Arize retains numeric quality columns when every row is scored; otherwise it exports labels with explicit status and preserves available values in explanations.

Implemented in six files under `evals/app/`:

- `judges.ts`: incomplete `jevShare` returns null; preserves valid readings, full `expectedItems`, and per-item `itemErrors`.
- `stats.ts`: boundary intervals use independent cluster counts; failed execution excludes quality from summaries, comparisons, and repeatability.
- `arize.ts`: harness success stays separate. Nullable quality columns become label-only with explicit status and preserved numeric values in explanations. Fully observed quality remains numeric.
- `reports.ts`: repeated-run quality averages exclude failures and select successful-run metadata when available.
- `stats.test.ts`, `evaluators.test.ts`: regression coverage for these behaviors.

Validation: **42 tests passed**, zero failures. No paid APIs called; live Arize upload was not tested. Coordinator-owned files and `agreement.ts` were untouched.
